web_evidence.title: In Five Years — Bookends Extract
web_evidence.note: A publisher-hosted 30-page extract sustains Dannie’s participating first-person narration throughout the opening chapters and future-vision scene.

web_evidence.title: In Five Years | Book by Rebecca Serle | Official Publisher Page
web_evidence.note: The official publisher excerpt opens with Dannie narrating her actions, perceptions, history, and relationship with David as “I.”

web_evidence.title: Rebecca Serle Writing Styles in In Five Years
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies Dannie Kohan as the novel’s exclusive first-person narrator and describes the final “After” section as a tense change, not a change of person.

web_evidence.title: A Tale of Mothers, Daughters, and Malibu: An Interview with Rebecca Serle about Once and Again
web_evidence.note: In a later author interview, Serle states that before Once and Again she had never written multiple viewpoints or third person and characterizes her earlier books as straight first-person narratives, corroborating In Five Years’ whole-book structure.

person_note: The event quotes repeatedly expose Dannie as a participating “I” narrator in specific present scenes, recollections, and character-specific habits. The official publisher extracts independently sustain the same first-person voice across the opening and vision sequence, while the whole-book study guide explicitly says Dannie narrates exclusively in first person. Serle’s later account of her earlier novels further rules against an alternating or third-person structure. Second-person examples in the quote set are dialogue or aphoristic address, and the verse passage is local material rather than evidence of another controlling narrator. No credible contrary evidence remains.
